title: Linked List Cycle Detection
statement: Implement `has_cycle(values, pos)` where `values` is the list sequence and `pos` is the index that the tail connects to (-1 means no cycle). Return True if a cycle exists. Use Floyd's algorithm mentally: slow moves 1, fast moves 2.
constraints: pos is -1 or a valid index

predict_steps.prompt: If slow and fast ever point to the same node, what does that mean?
predict_steps.hint: Fast lapped slow inside a loop.

learn_quiz.question: In Floyd's algorithm, fast moves how many steps?
If there is no cycle, fast will?
Meeting of slow and fast proves?

viva.question: How do fast and slow pointers detect a cycle in O(n) time and O(1) space?
What happens on an empty list or a single node without a self-loop?
Why must they eventually meet if a cycle exists?
expected_points: fast closes the gap inside the loop
